inputs.share_count_basis: Diluted weighted shares, Q2 2026 10-Q (481.389M). Held FLAT: SBC (incl. equity-award withholding) is fully expensed in the flows, so diluting the count too would double-charge it. ROL is a repurchaser (FY2025 ~$202M open-market buyback on top of ~$15M withholding; H1-2026 ~$28M), so the flat count is being funded, not just a modelling convention.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K cash-flow add-back $39.707M (XBRL ShareBasedCompensation) + ~$15M cash tax withheld on net-share settlement. ROL reports withholding inside 'Purchase of common stock' (XBRL PaymentsForRepurchaseOfCommonStock); the withholding portion is estimated from the H1-2025 figure ($14.9M, before the Q4-2025 open-market buyback). No combined SBC-plus-withholding figure is published. Same basis applied to history (FY2022 $7.1M, FY2020 $8.3M withholding).
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows. Risk-free 4.2% (10y UST), ERP 5.0%, beta 0.80 (defensive, recurring-service revenue; ROL's long-run beta is well below 1) -> cost of equity 8.2%. Debt ~$487M vs ~$14.7B market cap (~3% of capital) at ~5.8% pre-tax (FY2025 interest $28.6M) -> after-tax ~4.4%. WACC ~8.1%, rounded to 8.0%. Same WACC in every scenario: risk is carried by the scenario paths and weights, not by a per-scenario rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP ASC 842 operating leases (fleet vehicles, branches; FY2025 operating lease payments $159.1M) are expensed inside operating income and therefore inside EBITDA. Lease cost is in the flows; operating lease liabilities are therefore NOT in net debt. One treatment, applied once. lease_cost_pct_path is 0 because the charge is already inside the EBITDA margin.
inputs.acquisition_treatment: ROL is a serial acquirer ($310M FY2025, $157M FY2024, $367M FY2023; ~6.5% of revenue on average 2021-25, buying ~2.5-3pp of growth a year). Acquisitions are treated as NPV-neutral and excluded from BOTH sides: growth from FY2027 onward is ORGANIC only and no acquisition spend is charged. FY2026 (year 1) growth includes the inorganic contribution guided at 2-3%, because those deals (Romex $95.7M in Apr-2026, FY2025 Saela rollover) were paid for before the 2026-06-30 balance sheet that sets net debt; FY2027 carries a small Romex/H1-2026 rollover. Charging acquisition cash while also projecting acquired growth at ~2.3x sales prices would give roughly the same answer if deals earn ~WACC; any value creation from M&A above WACC is upside not in the base case.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF DCF, component route (dcf-methods routing: US operating company - recurring pest/termite services, asset-light, no bank/REIT/holdco features). First valuation of ROL; no prior DCF or memory entry. Owner FCF FY2025 = reported FCF 650.0 (OCF 678.1 - capex 28.1) - SBC incl. withholding 54.7 - interest income 0 (net debt, so no interest strip) = 595.3 (15.8% of revenue). EBITDA margin path is PRE-SBC adjusted EBITDA: FY2025 operating income 726.1 + D&A 124.7 + SBC 39.7 = 890.5 (23.7%); H1-2026 was 21.9% vs 23.1% in H1-2025 (Q2-26 operating margin -110bp on medical, fleet and fuel costs), so FY2026 is set at 22.8%. D&A of 3.3% is ~2.4pp acquired-intangible amortisation (FY2025 $90.4M), which is tax-deductible and rolls off over time absent new deals, hence the declining D&A path (it only matters through cash tax). Capex 0.75% of revenue (vehicles are leased). Cash tax 25% (FY2025 ETR 24.9%, cash taxes $162.9M on ~$701M pre-tax = 23.2%). Working capital: deferred revenue grows slowly with the book (+$7M FY2025) and is offset by receivables; wc_capture 0. Year-1 component check: owner FCF ~$655M on ~$4.08B revenue = 16.0%, vs 15.8% FY2025 actual - nothing unrepeatable is being carried forward. 10-year horizon because the base margin keeps expanding until ~Y8.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: organic revenue growth: FY2026 guidance 'at least 6%' organic, medium-term target 7-8%; the ex-M&A rate is used because the model charges no acquisition spend
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (2.7% 3yr / 7.3% 5yr) diverges by far more than 30% from revenue (11.7%) and EPS (13.3-15.1%). Book value is not the growth signal here: ROL pays out ~60% of earnings as dividends and spent $315M (FY2023 secondary-offering repurchase) and $217M (FY2025) on buybacks, so equity barely compounds. Revenue CAGR is itself inflated by ~3pp/yr of acquired revenue, so the selected rate is organic-only.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series = reported FCF - SBC - equity-award withholding: FY2020 383.4 (COVID tax/payroll deferrals inflate it), FY2022 407.0, FY2025 595.3. Owner-FCF CAGR (13.5% 3yr) runs slightly below reported (14.3%): SBC rose from 0.8% to 1.1% of revenue (1.45% incl. withholding) over FY2022-25, so a small and growing share of reported growth is paid in stock.

base.narrative: Guidance-anchored: FY2026 ~8.5% total growth (>=6% organic + 2-3% from deals already paid for), then organic 6-6.5% fading to 3.5% by Y10 - below the 7-8% medium-term target because the residential digital-lead funnel has not been shown to recover. Adjusted EBITDA margin recovers from the 2026 cost squeeze (22.8%) to 24.5% by Y8 on route density and the 30-35% incremental-margin target only partly delivered.

bull.narrative: Management's medium-term frame is delivered: residential lead generation recovers as Orkin re-tunes digital spend, organic growth returns to 7-8% with commercial (+8.6% in Q2-26) and termite/ancillary (+10.5%) staying strong, and 30-35% incremental EBITDA margins lift the margin to 26% as medical/fleet/fuel inflation normalises and integration synergies land.

bear.narrative: The residential softness is structural, not cyclical: search/AI-answer changes and rising ad costs keep Orkin's top-of-funnel weak, PE-backed roll-ups and Rentokil compete on price for local customers, and organic growth settles at 3-4% (price only). Medical, fleet, fuel and technician-wage inflation are not fully passed through, so the margin drifts to 22% and stays there.

scenario_narratives.base: Guidance-anchored: FY2026 ~8.5% total growth (>=6% organic plus 2-3% from deals already paid for), then 6-6.5% organic fading to 3.5% - below the 7-8% medium-term target because the residential digital-lead funnel that caused the Q2-26 miss has not been shown to recover. Commercial and termite/ancillary keep compounding. Margin recovers from the 2026 medical/fleet/fuel squeeze (22.8% adj. EBITDA) to 24.5% on route density, with the 30-35% incremental-margin target only partly delivered.
scenario_narratives.bull: Management's medium-term frame is delivered: Orkin's residential lead generation recovers, organic growth returns to 7-8% with commercial and termite/ancillary still leading, and 30-35% incremental margins lift adjusted EBITDA margin to 26% as cost inflation normalises and integration of 90+ deals over three years yields density and procurement gains.
scenario_narratives.bear: Residential softness is structural: changes in search and AI answer engines plus rising ad costs keep the Orkin top-of-funnel weak, PE-backed roll-ups and Rentokil compete on price and for targets, and organic growth settles at 3-4% (mostly price). Labour, medical, fleet and fuel inflation are only partly passed through, so the margin drifts to 22% and stays there. No balance-sheet stress: net debt is <0.5x EBITDA.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 20% because the Q2-26 miss came from the residential lead-generation funnel - a demand mechanism, not a one-off cost - and management cut organic guidance. Base 50% as the guidance-anchored path. Bull trimmed to 30% because it requires the residential recovery AND full delivery of the incremental-margin target; it is management's own stated frame, so it is not remote. No solvency or refinancing risk justifies a heavier bear.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Rollins is a high-quality, low-capital-intensity recurring-service compounder whose share price has roughly halved from its 52-week high on a residential demand miss. The valuation strips the acquisition engine out (organic growth only, no deal spend) so that the price is tested against what the existing route base earns, charges SBC plus equity-award withholding as a real cost, and caps the terminal value at 20x owner FCF.
key_risks_to_valuation: Residential organic growth: the Q2-26 miss was a lead-generation (digital/search) problem; if it persists, base-case 6-6.5% organic is too high
Margin: medical, fleet, fuel and wage inflation compressed Q2-26 operating margin 110bp; base assumes recovery to 24.5% adj. EBITDA
Terminal value is ~60%+ of EV and the 20x cap binds in the base and bull cases; a lower market multiple for slower-growth pest control would cut value directly
M&A treated as NPV-neutral: overpaying in a bid-up market for tuck-ins would destroy value the model does not charge; disciplined buying above WACC is unmodelled upside
Equity-award withholding is an estimate (~$15M) because ROL reports it inside its share-purchase line
